newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may challenge News Corp - Heritage Media deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may challenge News Corp - Heritage Media deal.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department may challenge News Corp.'s plans to acquire Heritage Media Corp. in a $1.35 billion stock-and-debt transaction, the two companies said on Monday.
The department's antitrust field office in San Francisco has recommended that the department challenge the deal, the companies said in a joint press release.
News Corp plans to buy Heritage, a Dallas-based mass marketing company, for $754 million in stock and the assumption of $600 million in debt. The deal was announced March 17.
The companies said they were told of the San Francisco field office's position after the close of U.S. stock market trading on Friday.
Justice Department staff have asked that Heritage and News Corp extend the period during which the antitrust division must either challenge the deal or allow it to close, they said.
News Corp and Heritage said they would grant the extension but would "vigorously pursue the approval of the acquisition by the Department of Justice."
